components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single forward action inside a decision area.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 44px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 8px); background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--action, oklch(73% 0.19 42)), var(--action-end, oklch(68% 0.22 35))); color: var(--on-action, oklch(18% 0.035 45)); padding: 10px 15px; font: 600 0.82rem/1.3 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI Variable', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; transition: background 180ms var(--ease-out, ease), transform 180ms var(--ease-out, ease); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: linear-gradient(135deg, oklch(77% 0.18 42), oklch(72% 0.21 35)); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent-strong, oklch(73% 0.19 42)); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.48; cursor: not-allowed; transform: none; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A quiet control for refresh, disclosure, navigation, and reversible actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { min-height: 39px; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong, oklch(76% 0.04 248 / 0.32)); border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 8px); background: var(--surface-soft, oklch(92% 0.02 250 / 0.045)); color: var(--text-soft, oklch(82% 0.018 250)); padding: 8px 14px; font: 600 0.75rem/1.3 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI Variable', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; transition: background 180ms var(--ease-out, ease), border-color 180ms var(--ease-out, ease), color 180ms var(--ease-out, ease); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--accent, oklch(64% 0.205 37)); background: var(--surface-hover, oklch(92% 0.02 250 / 0.082)); color: var(--text, oklch(96% 0.008 250)); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent-strong, oklch(73% 0.19 42)); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { opacity: 0.48; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: A recessed field with familiar focus treatment and readable help context.
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: grid; gap: 6px; color: var(--text-soft, oklch(82% 0.018 250)); font: 600 0.75rem/1.3 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI Variable', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-field { width: 100%; min-height: 39px; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(72% 0.035 248 / 0.18)); border-radius: 9px; background: var(--input, oklch(11.8% 0.026 252)); color: var(--text, oklch(96% 0.008 250)); padding: 8px 10px; font: 400 0.875rem/1.5 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI Variable', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; transition: border-color 140ms ease, background 140ms ease, box-shadow 140ms ease; } .ds-field::placeholder { color: var(--muted, oklch(68% 0.02 250)); } .ds-field:hover { border-color: var(--border-strong, oklch(76% 0.04 248 / 0.32)); } .ds-field:focus-visible { border-color: var(--accent, oklch(64% 0.205 37)); background: var(--surface-solid, oklch(15.5% 0.027 252)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--accent-soft, oklch(64% 0.205 37 / 0.14)); outline: 0; }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: A compact, non-action status marker whose text reinforces its color.
components.css: .ds-status-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(72% 0.035 248 / 0.18)); border-radius: 999px; background: var(--surface-soft, oklch(92% 0.02 250 / 0.045)); color: var(--text-soft, oklch(82% 0.018 250)); padding: 5px 9px; font: 600 0.75rem/1.3 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI Variable', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-status-dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--success, oklch(76% 0.12 157)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in srgb, var(--success, oklch(76% 0.12 157)) 13%, transparent); }

components.name: Structural Panel
components.description: One continuous Harbor Band split by a fine divider, not a stack of nested cards.
components.html:
Audit profile

components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 3px; overflow-x: auto; } .ds-nav-item { position: relative; min-height: 44px; border: 0; border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 8px); background: transparent; color: var(--muted, oklch(68% 0.02 250)); padding: 9px 12px; font: 600 0.82rem/1.3 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI Variable', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; white-space: nowrap; transition: color 180ms var(--ease-out, ease), background 180ms var(--ease-out, ease); cursor: pointer; } .ds-nav-item::after { position: absolute; right: 12px; bottom: 2px; left: 12px; height: 2px; background: var(--accent, oklch(64% 0.205 37)); content: ''; opacity: 0; transform: scaleX(0.5); transition: opacity 180ms var(--ease-out, ease), transform 180ms var(--ease-out, ease); } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: var(--surface-soft, oklch(92% 0.02 250 / 0.045)); color: var(--text-soft, oklch(82% 0.018 250)); } .ds-nav-item:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent-strong, oklch(73% 0.19 42)); outline-offset: -1px; } .ds-nav-item-active { color: var(--text, oklch(96% 0.008 250)); } .ds-nav-item-active::after { opacity: 1; transform: scaleX(1); }

components.name: Audit Phase Tab
components.description: A divider-led workflow tab that makes the current audit phase explicit.
components.css: .ds-phase-tab { position: relative; display: grid; min-width: 190px; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr; align-items: center; gap: 10px; border: 0; border-right: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(72% 0.035 248 / 0.18)); background: transparent; color: var(--muted, oklch(68% 0.02 250)); padding: 13px 15px; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; } .ds-phase-tab::after { position: absolute; right: 0; bottom: 0; left: 0; height: 2px; background: var(--accent, oklch(64% 0.205 37)); content: ''; opacity: 0; } .ds-phase-tab:hover { background: var(--surface-soft, oklch(92% 0.02 250 / 0.045)); color: var(--text-soft, oklch(82% 0.018 250)); } .ds-phase-tab:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--accent-strong, oklch(73% 0.19 42)); outline-offset: -3px; } .ds-phase-tab-active { color: var(--text, oklch(96% 0.008 250)); } .ds-phase-tab-active::after { opacity: 1; } .ds-phase-number { color: var(--accent, oklch(64% 0.205 37)); font: 700 0.75rem/1 ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; } .ds-phase-tab strong, .ds-phase-tab small { display: block; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI Variable', 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; } .ds-phase-tab strong { font-size: 0.82rem; } .ds-phase-tab small { margin-top: 3px; color: var(--muted, oklch(68% 0.02 250)); font-size: 0.72rem; }

narrative.overview:
ScopeHarbor should feel like a calm security workspace in a dim office or home environment: focused enough for meaningful AppSec work, clear enough for a solo developer to use without specialist coaching, and polished enough that dense evidence feels ordered. A restrained orange signal traces the authorized path from scope to profile, scan, finding, and remediation. It is a guide through the work, not decoration around it.

The canvas is a near-black, blue-tinted neutral field with one continuous structural surface for each major product band. Fine dividers organize related content; nested navy cards do not. The interface becomes dense only when evidence earns that density. Before data exists, loading and empty states explain the prerequisite and the next useful action.

The system explicitly rejects the look and behavior of a hacker-themed terminal, an intimidating expert-only scanner, and security theater that hides the workflow. Familiar controls, direct language, restrained motion, and visible safety boundaries create trust.
keyCharacteristics: A dark ambient canvas with restrained orange used as a navigational signal.
Continuous surfaces divided by fine lines instead of stacks of bubbly cards.
Sleek system typography with compact, readable hierarchy and bounded prose.
Explicit audit phases, prerequisites, status feedback, and next actions.
A secure-network WebGL hero that supports the workflow without controlling it.
Progressive disclosure for findings, activity, comparisons, reports, and explanations.

rules.name: The Orange Thread Rule
rules.body: Orange must remain a scarce directional signal. Use it for the current step, the primary action, selected state, and hero network—not for headings, decorative illustrations, or whole dashboard sections.

rules.name: The Signal Sprinkle Rule
rules.body: Blue and amber may appear in progress bars, comparison details, and live state indicators. They must not recolor section titles, navigation icons, or general imagery.

rules.name: The Structural Navy Rule
rules.body: One navy-tinted band may contain several related sections. Separate them with one-pixel dividers; never place every subdivision inside another navy card.

rules.name: The Sleek Utility Rule
rules.body: Use one interface sans family across the product. Bubbly display faces, pseudo-terminal typography, and decorative font pairings are prohibited.

rules.name: The Read-It-Once Rule
rules.body: A section gets a title and one concise explanatory sentence when its purpose or prerequisite is not obvious. Explanations must not compete with the task or repeat nearby labels.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Depth begins with tone and a one-pixel divider. If a section reads clearly without a shadow, the shadow is forbidden.

rules.name: The No Ghost-Card Rule
rules.body: Never pair a one-pixel border with a broad decorative shadow. Panels use compact structural depth; internal panes use dividers and no shadow.

dos: Do make authorized scope, active profile, workflow status, and the next action visible at every audit phase.
Do use Signal Orange for the current path and primary action, while keeping most of the screen neutral.
Do use one continuous Harbor Band with internal one-pixel dividers for related content.
Do add one concise description wherever a prerequisite, consequence, or unfamiliar security concept would otherwise force the user to guess.
Do use purposeful loading and empty states that teach the next step.
Do bound long findings, comparisons, activity, reports, and explanations with sorting, pagination, or progressive disclosure.
Do preserve visible focus, keyboard operation, WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, non-color status cues, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep the secure-network hero polished, orange-led, and subordinate to the audit workflow.
Do preserve semantic light-theme mappings whenever a dark-theme token changes.
donts: Don't make ScopeHarbor resemble a hacker-themed terminal or an intimidating expert-only scanner.
Don't hide the workflow behind security theater, unexplained specialist knowledge, raw scanner noise, or uncertain next steps.
Don't color headings, general header icons, or large illustrations blue, amber, or orange; color belongs to actions and data-bearing features.
Don't create a patchwork of navy cards. If every subdivision has its own filled rectangle, the hierarchy is wrong.
Don't use bubbly containers, oversized radii, pill-shaped sections, or bubble separators. Prefer straight edges, modest corners, and lines.
Don't use nested cards, identical icon-card grids, colored side-stripe borders, gradient text, decorative glassmorphism, or decorative grid backgrounds.
Don't use mono typography as the product voice, add fake command prompts, or expose raw tool output for atmosphere.
Don't show every result or explanation at once when a bounded preview communicates the set.
Don't let text overflow, truncate essential security meaning, or shrink body text to solve a layout problem.
Don't rely on motion, WebGL, or color alone to communicate readiness, severity, completion, or permission.
